records.editorial_note: Editorial variable correction: the official paper prints F(x) < a for every rational a, with x unbound. The bank uses F(a) < a, matching the variable quantified in that clause. This is an editorial restoration, not an official erratum.
The Hebrew phrase that each set contains 502 (respectively 251) points is translated as at least that many points; it does not assert that the sets have exactly those cardinalities.

Editorial domain clarification: every club must have at least one member in both parts. The source explicitly states this in part (b), but omits it in part (a); allowing empty clubs makes part (a) false.
Editorial degeneracy clarification: angles of 0 degrees are allowed. The source says acute angles without excluding collinear point sets; a strictly positive-angle reading fails for a collinear set.
The initial statement on page 2 uses 10^20 - 1. The authors explicitly replace it with 10^20 - 9 on page 3. The bank follows that official corrected restatement.

The official statement does not specify a starting point on an extended side line or the orientation of each associated line direction. Its wording is retained; the region construction is understood where it is defined. Source comparison does not certify these omitted boundary conventions.

records.editorial_note: Editorial domain clarification: n >= 3 is required because the question asks for three distinct points. The official question omits a range for n. All ten answer expressions are retained. Their ordering changes for small n; the source does not specify a uniform or asymptotic comparison, which remains a source ambiguity.
